title: Effects of harvest and fertilization frequency on protein yield and extractability from flood-tolerant perennial grasses cultivated on a fen peatland
source_location: Table 1; article Methods: Site Description and Experimental Design; article lines/table text verified 2026-11-07
license: Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY), as stated in the article
experimental_design: Four-block field experiment on a fen peatland; reed canary grass and tall fescue; one through five harvests; reported annual-average rows and per-harvest rows.

units.dm_yield_mean_t_dm_ha: t dry matter per hectare for the reported harvest; annual-average records are t dry matter per hectare per year
units.dm_yield_sd_t_dm_ha: source-reported standard deviation in the corresponding yield unit
units.crude_protein_mean_g_kg_dm: g crude protein per kg dry matter
units.crude_protein_sd_g_kg_dm: source-reported standard deviation in g/kg dry matter
units.harvest_week: week number reported by the study; not converted to a date or month

transformation: Table 1 means and parenthetical standard deviations transcribed as separate numeric fields. Annual-average rows are retained separately from individual harvest rows. No conversion, interpolation, reweighting, or imputation applied.
applicability: Evidence for harvest timing and composition-yield coupling in cultivated flood-tolerant grasses; only a qualitative/analogue reference for roadside feedstock.
limitations: Cultivated reed canary grass and tall fescue on fen peatland are not mixed roadside verge grass.

The one-cut regime received 100 kg N and K per hectare per year; two- to five-cut regimes received 200 kg N and K per hectare per year. Harvest frequency and fertilizer regime are therefore confounded.
The study's seasonal harvest weeks are not transferable directly to Dutch roadside mowing calendars.
Annual-average values are study-reported means; SDs are not sums of cut-level SDs.
Table 1 does not provide GreenHub site-area availability, delivered fresh-mass yield, collection losses, or route-level costs.
The authors state raw data are available from authors; this extract contains published table values, not replicate-level data.
